Faq.title: Frequently asked questions
Faq.description: The questions we get most often: who we are, how we install and what happens after the purchase.

items.title: Who is Rayforce?
items.answer: We are the EV charging line of Bamibel S.A., a Uruguayan engineering company with over 25 years of experience. That track record stands behind every unit and every installation.

items.title: Are your units authorized by URSEA?
items.answer: Yes. Our full line of chargers for cars and trucks is registered with URSEA under authorization VU-SE-17-000123. The registry is public and you can look it up.

items.title: Who does the installation?
items.answer: We do, in house. We never subcontract: our engineers and UTE-certified electricians install every unit following Uruguayan electrical code.

items.title: What warranty do the units carry?
items.answer: One year of warranty, handled directly by us here in Uruguay. You do not depend on overseas service or a middleman importer.

items.title: What areas do you cover?
items.answer: We install in Montevideo and across the country. If you are outside the metro area, get in touch and we will arrange the site visit and timeline.

items.title: How can I pay?
items.answer: You can buy directly through MercadoPago on this site, or message us on WhatsApp to arrange other payment methods and get a quote with installation included.

items.title: Do you work with businesses, buildings and fleets?
items.answer: Yes. We handle projects for businesses, parking facilities, buildings and fleets, with 7, 11 and 22 kW units. Get in touch and we will scope it against your existing installation.

items.title: What happens after the purchase?
items.answer: You get local technical support: commissioning, Rayforce app setup and any questions afterwards. You message us and we handle it ourselves.

Faq.title: Frequently asked questions
Faq.description: What people ask us most about the Rayforce Besen BS20 chargers before choosing a model.

items.title: Which power level should I choose, 7.2kW, 11kW or 22kW?
items.answer: It depends on your electrical supply. With single-phase — the most common setup in a home — the cap is 7.2kW. The 11 and 22kW need a three-phase supply: without one, they won't deliver that power no matter what the unit supports.

items.title: Integrated cable or Type 2 socket?
items.answer: Integrated cable if the charger is for your own car: charging is unhooking the cable, nothing loose in the garage. Type 2 socket if more than one car will use it, since each arrives with its own — but the cable isn't included there.

items.title: Does a higher-kW charger always charge faster?
items.answer: Not if your supply can't match it. A 22kW on a single-phase supply charges at the same speed as a 7.2kW: the real power is capped by the supply, not the charger.

items.title: Are the chargers approved by URSEA?
items.answer: Yes, the whole BS20 line is registered with URSEA under authorization VU-SE-17-000123. It's a public registry and you can check it.

items.title: What's the difference between residential and commercial use?
items.answer: Power and the supply it needs. The 7.2kW covers a home's daily use; the 11 and 22kW are built for where the car rotates between several drivers, like a business or a fleet, and they need a three-phase supply.

items.title: Do they come with an app?
items.answer: Yes, every model is controlled through the Rayforce app: start and stop charging, and check your consumption from your phone.

items.title: What's the warranty on the charger?
items.answer: One year, which we handle ourselves here in Uruguay — you don't depend on a service center abroad.

items.title: Is installation included in the price?
items.answer: You can choose: buy just the unit, or add installation by our UTE-certified electricians. That option is set at checkout.

bs20-bc-7kw.title: Frequently asked questions
bs20-bc-7kw.description: What people ask us most about the single-phase 7.2kW wallbox with integrated cable.

items.title: Will it work with the wiring I already have?
items.answer: In most homes, yes: the unit is single-phase 220V and draws 32A, which is what a standard house supplies. What it does need is a dedicated line from the panel with its own breaker, rather than sharing a circuit that already feeds something else. Our electrician checks this before installing.

items.title: How long does a charge take?
items.answer: At 7.2kW, roughly 7 to 9 hours to take a mid-sized battery from 0 to 100%. In practice nobody starts from empty: you plug in when you get home and it's full by morning. Against a standard outlet, which gives about 2kW, it's three to four times faster.

items.title: Is 6 meters of cable enough?
items.answer: For a garage or a covered carport, almost always. The 6 meters run from where the unit is mounted to the connector, so what matters is where the wall sits relative to your car's charging port. If you're unsure, send us a photo of the spot and we'll tell you.

items.title: Can I mount it outdoors?
items.answer: Yes. It's IP66: it stands up to water and dust, and works between -25°C and +55°C. That said, under cover both the unit and the connector age better.

items.title: What can I do from the app?
items.answer: Start and stop charging, see the consumption of each session, and schedule when it charges. It connects over Bluetooth, and the unit has its own display, so you can also operate it without your phone.

items.title: Is it URSEA approved?
items.answer: Yes, the entire BS20 line is registered with URSEA under authorization VU-SE-17-000123. It's a public registry and you can look it up.

items.title: Is installation included?
items.answer: You choose: buy the unit on its own, or add installation by our UTE-certified electricians. You pick the option in the same purchase, up in the pricing section.

items.title: What warranty does it come with?
items.answer: One year, handled directly by us here in Uruguay — you're not waiting on a service center abroad.

bs20-bc-11kw.title: Frequently asked questions
bs20-bc-11kw.description: What people ask us most about the three-phase 11kW wallbox with integrated cable.

items.title: Do I need a three-phase supply?
items.answer: Yes. This unit runs at 400V across three phases, 16A per phase. Without three-phase power there's no way for it to deliver 11kW: if your home is single-phase, the right model is the 7.2kW.

items.title: How do I know if I have three-phase?
items.answer: Check your UTE bill or your panel: on three-phase you'll see three live lines plus neutral, and the contracted capacity is listed in kW rather than amps on a single line. If you're not sure, send us a photo of the panel and we'll confirm it before you buy.

items.title: Why 11kW instead of 22kW?
items.answer: Because 11kW is the point where the power is useful without demanding a large contract. A 22kW unit needs considerably more contracted capacity to actually perform, and in a house or a small business that contract costs more than it gives back. Outside of a fleet or a building garage, 11kW is the practical three-phase choice.

items.title: How long does a charge take?
items.answer: At 11kW, around 4 to 6 hours to take a mid-sized battery from 0 to 100% — about half what a 7.2kW single-phase unit takes. The real ceiling is your car's onboard charger: if yours accepts up to 7.4kW, that's what it will draw no matter what the wallbox offers.

items.title: Is 6 meters of cable enough?
items.answer: For a garage or a covered carport, almost always. The 6 meters run from where the unit is mounted to the connector, so what matters is where the wall sits relative to your car's charging port. If you're unsure, send us a photo of the spot and we'll tell you.

items.title: Can I mount it outdoors?
items.answer: Yes. It's IP66: it stands up to water and dust, and works between -25°C and +55°C. That said, under cover both the unit and the connector age better.

items.title: What can I do from the app?
items.answer: Start and stop charging, see the consumption of each session, and schedule when it charges. It connects over Bluetooth, and the unit has its own display, so you can also operate it without your phone.

items.title: Is it URSEA approved?
items.answer: Yes, the entire BS20 line is registered with URSEA under authorization VU-SE-17-000123. It's a public registry and you can look it up.

items.title: Is installation included?
items.answer: You choose: buy the unit on its own, or add installation by our UTE-certified electricians. On three-phase we recommend installing with us: wiring the three phases and their protection isn't a job to take on without a certified electrician.

items.title: What warranty does it come with?
items.answer: One year, handled directly by us here in Uruguay — you're not waiting on a service center abroad.

bs20-bc-22kw.title: Frequently asked questions
bs20-bc-22kw.description: What people ask us most about the three-phase 22kW wallbox for businesses, buildings and fleets.

items.title: Do I need a three-phase supply?
items.answer: Yes, and a sizeable one. The unit runs at 400V across three phases, 32A per phase. Without three-phase power it won't deliver 22kW no matter what the unit supports, and neither will it on a small contract: before selling you one, we confirm your UTE contract actually makes use of it.

items.title: Does it make sense at home?
items.answer: Usually not. The capacity a home typically contracts leaves real-world charging well below 22kW, so you'd be paying for power you won't use. For a house, the 7.2kW covers each night's charge and costs less.

items.title: Who is this model for?
items.answer: Building garages, businesses and fleets: places where the car rotates between several drivers and each one needs to leave charged quickly. That's where the full 22kW gets used.

items.title: How long does a charge take?
items.answer: At 22kW, around 2 to 3 hours to take a mid-sized battery from 0 to 100%. The real ceiling is your car's onboard charger: many EVs accept up to 11kW on AC, so that's what they'll draw no matter what the wallbox offers.

items.title: Can I install several in the same place?
items.answer: Yes, that's the typical case in a building or a fleet. What needs sizing is the panel and the contracted capacity, so that several units charging at once don't exceed it. Write to us and we'll work out the layout with your electrician.

items.title: Can I mount it outdoors?
items.answer: Yes. It's IP66: it stands up to water and dust, and works between -25°C and +55°C, which is what an open garage or a parking lot asks of it.

items.title: What can I do from the app?
items.answer: Start and stop charging, see the consumption of each session, and schedule when it charges. It connects over Bluetooth, and the unit has its own display, so you can also operate it without your phone.

items.title: Is it URSEA approved?
items.answer: Yes, the entire BS20 line is registered with URSEA under authorization VU-SE-17-000123. It's a public registry and you can look it up.

items.title: Is installation included?
items.answer: You choose: buy the unit on its own, or add installation by our UTE-certified electricians. On a 22kW unit we recommend installing with us: wiring the three phases and their protection isn't a job to take on without a certified electrician.

items.title: What warranty does it come with?
items.answer: One year, handled directly by us here in Uruguay — you're not waiting on a service center abroad.

Faq.title: Frequently asked questions
Faq.description: What we get asked most about charging cables before choosing length and connector.

items.title: What cable length do I need?
items.answer: All three models are 5 metres, which covers most situations: it reaches from the charge point to a car parked beside it or facing the other way. If your setup needs more length, message us and we will see what we can source.

items.title: Straight or coiled?
items.answer: The coiled one retracts on its own and stays gathered: it takes up less room and does not drag on the floor. The straight one is lighter and easier to coil up for the boot. If the cable lives in the garage, go coiled; if you carry it in the car, go straight.

items.title: Will it work with my car?
items.answer: If your car is Type 2 — the European standard, which covers almost every EV sold in Uruguay — yes. Open any of the models above and you will find the compatibility check by make and model.

items.title: 7kW or 22kW?
items.answer: It depends on your installation, not on the cable. All three handle 32A: the 7kW is single-phase and the 22kW is three-phase. If your home is single-phase — the usual case — the 7kW is the one for you. The 22kW only pays off with a three-phase supply and a charger that uses it; on single-phase it will not charge any faster.

items.title: Can I use this cable at public chargers?
items.answer: Yes, that is exactly what it is for. Public AC chargers in Uruguay have a Type 2 socket and no cable: you bring your own and plug one end into the post and the other into the car.

items.title: Is it safe to leave outdoors?
items.answer: Yes. The connectors are IP66, which is rain and dust resistant, and they carry a temperature sensor that cuts off if anything overheats. Still, put it away when not in use: constant sun shortens the life of the sheath.

items.title: Does it have a warranty?
items.answer: Yes, every cable comes with a warranty and local support. If anything fails, message us and we sort it out here, with no paperwork abroad.
